name: Caiaphas
bio: After Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead, the chief priests and Pharisees met in council, worried that letting Jesus continue would lead all to believe in him and bring Roman retaliation on the nation; Caiaphas, high priest that year, told them it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish, a statement John notes unknowingly prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and indeed for the scattered children of God everywhere. From that day the council determined to kill Jesus (John 11:47-53). Caiaphas, the high priest, hosted the chief priests and elders at his palace as they plotted to arrest and kill Jesus by stealth, avoiding the feast days to prevent an uproar among the people (Matthew 26:3-5). His role presiding over Jesus's trial is told in detail in the chapters ahead. Jesus was brought to Caiaphas's house, where the council sought false testimony against him. When Jesus admitted under direct questioning that he was the Christ, Caiaphas tore his robes, declared it blasphemy, and led the council in condemning him to death (Matthew 26:57-68).
